mission.display_title: Construct a confidence interval for an unknown parameter from a random sample
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to construct a confidence interval for an unknown parameter of a distribution based on a random sample — so the CI coverage reading is usable — without pretending prediction intervals (3.2.2) are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to state a CI for a parameter from sample evidence and refuse treating a prediction interval as today's LO.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from random-sample evidence to a parameter confidence interval under CMP language.
mission.learning_objective: Confidence interval for an unknown parameter of a distribution based on a random sample.
mission.concept_focus: Random sample → estimator / pivotal idea → parameter CI → refuse prediction-as-done.
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Kappa closed estimators (3.1) with Revision. Today opens topic 3.2 at LO 3.2.1 — the named Continuity Front after CS1-010.
mission.why_now: 3.2.1 is the lawful Continuity Front after Kappa. Closing it prevents a cliff at intervals while keeping prediction intervals as day two.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for parameter CI — not Topic Complete for 3.2.2.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Lambda Day 1 because CE-001 / EP-001 Continuity Front names 3.2 as the handoff from Kappa.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What does a confidence interval claim about an unknown parameter? (2) What sample ingredient enters the construction? (3) Name one reason a prediction interval is not today's LO.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: A confidence interval uses random-sample evidence to give an interval for an unknown parameter with a stated frequentist coverage reading. A prediction interval targets a future observation — that is tomorrow's LO, not today's.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A colleague says 'I wrote a prediction interval, so I finished today's LO.' Refuse in one sentence and restate what today's LO requires.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse: prediction interval is tomorrow's LO. Today requires a confidence interval for an unknown parameter based on a random sample.
